title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive
source_used: The Register (reporting on a Gartner forecast)
key_facts: Gartner predicts more than half of quantum computing startups will be out of business by 2030.
It expects customers to reject technologies that do not achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing.
There are an estimated 200 to 300 quantum startups; Gartner forecasts $1.1 billion in worldwide quantum revenue in 2027, up from $869.9 million forecast for this year.
Public sector spending is forecast at $245 million in 2027, up from $219 million this year; banking, finance and insurance are expected to overtake it in 2028 ($289 million against $280 million).
Gartner says the "early quantum advantage era" has arrived because current processors can do limited complex tasks with better error reduction, while broad commercial usefulness remains elusive.
Gaurav Gupta of Gartner advised IT leaders to treat quantum as a multi-year effort.
quote_evidence: More than half of quantum computing startups will be out of business by 2030, Gartner predicts, as an overcrowded market struggles to generate enough commercial revenue.
Estimates put the number of quantum startups at between 200 and 300, competing in a market Gartner forecasts will generate $1.1 billion in worldwide revenue in 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: An analyst firm forecasts a shakeout among quantum startups.
notes: Analyst prediction reported by The Register, which adds its own view on the DOE 2028 goal (not used). Gartner's report itself was not opened.
